summary: Earth Jukebox is an accessible web application that transforms NASA Earth data into dynamic, real-time soundscapes (sonification). By mapping critical climate variables—such as global temperature, Arctic sea ice, wildfires, and CO₂ levels—to musical parameters like pitch, volume, and rhythm, the app makes complex scientific trends accessible to blind and low-vision users. It bridges the gap between data and the senses, proving that science can be heard, not just seen.
details:
The Problem: At least 2.2 billion people worldwide have vision impairment. NASA’s Earth Information Center publishes stunning visualizations daily, but they are exclusively visual. Even sighted users often skim past charts without truly feeling the urgency of climate change.

The Solution: Earth Jukebox translates sight into sound. Users can select specific Earth data tracks (Temperature, Sea Ice, Wildfires, CO₂) and immediately hear a generated soundscape. For example, rising temperatures produce ascending notes, while melting ice produces fading tones.

How it works: Each data value is mapped to a note on a pentatonic musical scale. Data intensity is mapped to volume, and the data type dictates the waveform (e.g., a low drone for CO₂). The audio is synthesized in real-time using the Web Audio API, ensuring no audio files are required.

Accessibility First: The interface features screen-reader optimized descriptions, full keyboard operability, aria-live announcements, and high-contrast UI with reduced-motion support.
